objective: Produce schema-conformant deterministic WorldState snapshots from validated ordered WorldEvents while preserving the World Model's existing internal reducer and verifier state. Repair PR #279 location-evidence binding and whitespace location IDs on current main.
decision_supported: Can an accepted WorldEvent stream be replayed into a contract-valid, hash-addressable WorldState snapshot with identical hashes across independent processes and without changing interfaces or robot behavior?
outputs: Pydantic WorldState, WorldStateEntity and WorldStateRelation models matching the current repository schema.
A World Model-owned deterministic snapshot projection that preserves the existing internal reducer and verifier API.
Documented canonical UTF-8 JSON bytes and SHA-256 exclusion rules.
Typed Observation entity_type validation with fail-closed persistence and replay behavior.
Unit and integration evidence for schema validation, hash sensitivity, metadata exclusion and cross-process stability.
acceptance: The shared contracts package exposes strict Pydantic WorldState, entity and relation models matching the current world_state.schema.json without modifying interfaces.
Every Observation WorldEvent requires a non-blank string entity_type; missing, blank and non-string values fail before SQLite insertion or reducer mutation.
Legacy persisted Observation payloads without entity_type fail closed during read or replay and are not silently migrated.
Conflicting entity_type values for the same entity_id are rejected during full-stream preflight before any event is applied.
The existing internal reducer WorldState and verifier-facing fields remain compatible; a separate explicit snapshot projection returns the contract WorldState.
The public snapshot validates through both the repository JSON Schema and the shared Pydantic model.
Snapshot entities are deterministically ordered by entity_id and relations are deterministically ordered by subject_id, predicate and object_id.

Canonical in:<entity_id> and on:<entity_id> locations project to inside and on_top_of relations; an unrepresentable non-empty location fails snapshot creation instead of being guessed or silently omitted.
Snapshot sequence_no is the highest accepted sequence boundary after exact duplicate folding, including the schema minimum boundary of zero.
Snapshot reduced_at is derived from the highest-sequence accepted event occurred_at; reverse timestamp order never changes replay order.
Canonical hash bytes are UTF-8 JSON encoded with sorted keys, compact separators, finite JSON values and deterministic collection order.
Canonical hash material contains run_id, sequence_no, entities and relations and excludes state_hash, reduced_at and clock_id.
Identical accepted streams produce identical state_hash values for every input permutation and in two independent Python processes.
Changing a schema-visible semantic field changes state_hash.
Optional missing pose or location does not invent data; the corresponding optional snapshot field or relation is omitted.
An empty event stream retains the existing internal reduce_events behavior but public snapshot creation fails closed because no truthful reduced_at boundary exists.
The integration replay test asserts a real non-empty 64-character lowercase SHA-256 state_hash rather than leaving the assertion commented out.
The scripted demo supplies entity_type for every Observation and uses canonical location syntax without changing planning, robot control or verification ownership.

Spatial verification requires dedicated evidence for every location used in a conclusion; generic entity or appearance evidence cannot fill a missing location-evidence slot. Attribute-only policy conclusions retain their attribute evidence behavior.

Confirmed and refuted spatial results cite only the relevant current location evidence; later appearance-only observations cannot substitute for it. Compound parcel policy success may also cite relevant attribute evidence, but only after its independent location-evidence requirement passes.
Location changes replace dedicated location evidence; repeated same-location observations accumulate deduplicated support. Unsupported extra-entity locations cannot establish refutation.
Snapshot relation object IDs reject ASCII or Unicode whitespace anywhere instead of silently trimming or normalizing IDs. Canonical in:<id> and on:<id> remain accepted.

risks_and_fallbacks: The current public WorldState schema cannot represent internal entity_attributes; the bounded fallback is to preserve them internally and exclude them from the public snapshot and hash.
Changing the existing reduce_events return type would create a broad verifier migration; the bounded fallback is a separate explicit snapshot projection using the same validated ordered stream.
Existing legacy Observation events without entity_type will fail closed; recovery requires an explicitly approved offline migration task rather than silent defaults.
The current WorldEvent Python contract does not expose clock_id although the JSON Schema permits it; the bounded implementation omits optional snapshot clock_id and excludes it from hash material.
A non-canonical location cannot be represented faithfully as a schema relation; the bounded fallback is to reject snapshot creation and request an explicitly scoped location-contract decision.
Rollback consists of removing the new snapshot projection and shared WorldState exports while retaining the existing internal reducer behavior.

Runtime/Contracts and bounded Integration scope retain the human approvals recorded in the implementation conversation; the human World Model Owner requested the PR #279 repair including verifier.py. Request those Owners again for final PR review.

Internal manually constructed states must supply entity_location_evidence_refs for spatial claims; there is no fallback to generic entity evidence. No legacy database migration or Issue #62/#165 freshness/metadata work is included.
